::: {.callout-tip title="Further reading"}
- @zhou2024matrix, sections 6 ("Linear functions and operators")
  and 7 ("Affine functions"),
  proves that every linear function is a matrix-vector product
  by the same route as @thm-linear-map-matrix,
  and that every affine function has the form $\matr{A}\vx + \vec{b}$.
  It defines "affine" differently, by
  $f(\alpha \vx + \beta \vy) = \alpha f(\vx) + \beta f(\vy)$
  whenever $\alpha + \beta = 1$,
  and shows that this condition holds exactly for the maps $\matr{A}\vx + \vec{b}$,
  so the two definitions agree.
- @boyd2018vmls, chapter 2 ("Linear functions"),
  covers the vector-to-number case:
  linear functions as inner products, affine functions,
  the [first-order Taylor approximation](calculus.qmd#def-linear-approximation) as an affine function,
  and the regression model.
  Section 8.1 ("Linear and affine functions")
  covers the vector-to-vector case.
  A free PDF is on the book's website.
:::
